lead_headline: Weekend restaurant tracker adds 9 leads (5 openings, 4 closures) including Vaultaire's subterranean HiFi bar debut beneath La Forêt and FiNO's Med tapas at renovated All Inn—liquor freeze hits day 37

restaurant.blurb: 9 new leads since Friday (5 openings, 4 closures) push active inventory to 88 cases—weekend highlights include Vaultaire launching Saturday as subterranean HiFi listening bar beneath La Forêt on Broadway (vintage spirits, analog sound, confidence 10), FiNO opening Mediterranean coastal tapas Friday inside renovated All Inn Hotel at Colfax/City Park (soft launch confidence 10), Paperboy Denver bringing Austin brunch brand's first Texas exit to West Highland (confidence 10). Closures: Super Mega Bien shuttered March 14 after 8-year RiNo run citing financial pressures despite 4.6-star reviews (confidence 10), Chances Grill Denver closed at Market Street nightclub/Caribbean spot (confidence 9). Weekend also tagged Wash Park Social opening at former Grille site, Roll It Up Sushi claiming Edgewater Public Market stall, plus backfill reclassifications for Riot House nightclub and Bar Amorina cocktail bar. Three-day window favors upscale concepts (HiFi bars, coastal Med) over casual closures, extending Union Station corridor dominance from prior week.

foreclosure.blurb: 48 filings this week climb 37% from last week's 35, with Douglas County's $1.1M Beebalm Loop property leading the roster—no $2M+ cases as 92 auctions line up next seven days.

liquor.blurb: Zero applications today extend statewide filing void to 37 consecutive days—Monday marks seventh straight zero-filing day as April's opening week posts 0/7 goose egg, now 208% beyond December 2024's 12-day record and obliterating all database precedent. No regulatory announcements, no social chatter, no legislative freeze evidence—backlog estimate climbs to 75-100 applications as system paralysis enters sixth week with zero official acknowledgment across Liquor Enforcement Division channels or statehouse tracking.

reputation.blurb: 1 mention today closes weekend at 59 citations (+7% vs prior week's 55) across 16 sources—week's haul led by Instagram (15 mentions), Denver Post (13), Facebook (11), with social platforms commanding 46% share. Recent pickups include Facebook homelessness housing thread, Instagram Cherry Creek fashion coverage, tatianawidmann.de parking policy analysis. Source diversity holds flat at 16 vs prior week while mention volume ticks up modestly, extending March-to-April acceleration (59 vs 54/week average) though still trailing February's 4.1/day peak.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +2 since Friday (2 new, 0 canceled) nudges MTD to −1 (−0.2/day) while 90-day net holds +136. Weekend's zero-churn bump follows Thursday-Friday flatline—past week delivers +4 net (18 new, 14 canceled) vs prior week's +20 (34 new, 14 canceled), marking 80% acquisition slowdown. Six-day April start posts +1 net (13 new, 10 canceled, 0.2/day) versus March's opening sextet (+22 net, 3.7/day), confirming 95% deceleration. YTD +130 (+1.4/day) cushions monthly stumble, but current 0.2/day April pace projects +5 month-end net—needs 26-subscriber acceleration to match Q1's +1.4/day average, signaling seasonal headwinds or conversion friction requiring intervention.
